title: Anthropic opens Claude Duet, an agent that asks before it acts; Apple Music unveils a logo shaped by sound
dek: Claude Duet and the ask-or-act question, Apple Music's new identity, VS Code's redesign as a case study, how Randy Hunt runs small teams, and two events.
preheader: Claude Duet asks before it acts, Apple Music's logo is shaped by sound, and how VS Code refreshed its UI.
hero_alt: Basic shapes stacked into a balancing tower under a circle sun
summary: Anthropic [opened a research preview of Claude Duet](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/21/anthropic-takes-on-chatgpt-dots-and-meta-muse-with-claude-duet/), a proactive agent that sends a morning brief, keeps working in the background and asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes anything. Early testers like [Claire Vo find it polished but too quiet](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/claude-duet-is-beautiful-i-still) to become a habit, and Jakob Nielsen's [latest roundup](https://jakobnielsenphd.substack.com/p/ux-roundup-20261019) adds a rule every agent needs: a reliable way to stop a run without losing finished work. Apple Music [unveiled a new identity with a logo shaped by sound](https://9to5mac.com/2026/10/21/apple-music-unveils-new-design-rebrand-with-logo-made-by-sound/), arriving with iOS 27.2 next week. And today's case study is the [VS Code team's modern UI rollout](https://code.visualstudio.com/blogs/2026/10/15/modern-ui), a lesson in refreshing a tool people use all day without breaking their muscle memory.

reads.title: Anthropic takes on ChatGPT Dots and Meta Muse with Claude Duet
reads.note: A morning brief, a Tasks tab only you can close, and a firm rule to ask before sending, paying, signing or deleting: a useful reference model for designing agent permissions.

reads.title: Claude Duet is beautiful. I still forgot to use it
reads.note: Claire Vo praises the onboarding, task lists and first-class artifacts, then argues that an agent which rarely nudges you never becomes a habit, and that latency kills back-and-forth work.

reads.title: UX roundup: AI by design phase
reads.note: A survey of 443 designers finds AI use peaks in discovery (72%) and falls in delivery (41%); a randomised Figma Make study saw AI cut product managers' task time twice as much as designers'.

reads.note: The logo was physically shaped by a Fred again.. composition with NEST Acoustics and captured in camera; users see the new look in iOS 27.2 next week.

case.title: Modernizing the VS Code UI
case.note: A decade of one-at-a-time features had left the workbench inconsistent, so the team built shared tokens for spacing, size and colour, tried them first in the new Agents window, then rolled out through Insiders and a controlled Stable experiment. The decision that made it work: when users said a roomier layout meant less code on screen, the team added a Compact density instead of reverting, and kept the classic UI one setting away.

learn.title: Randy Hunt keeps design teams small on purpose

person.name: Randy Hunt
person.role: Design leader at Notion and Etsy

learn.intro: Randy Hunt has led design at Notion and Etsy, and on Design Better he explains why his teams stay smaller and flatter than people expect, and why he shields good people from busywork.
steps: Keep the team deliberately small, so limited bandwidth forces you to choose what matters instead of doing everything.
Have designers ship code to production, as he set up at Etsy in 2010, long before design engineer was a common title.
Give small touchpoints like push notifications the same care as the main dashboard, an approach he calls whole design.
learn.source_line: From Design Better, episode 194 · our takeaways from the episode page
learn.take: These habits come from the episode's published summary; the full conversation is for paid subscribers.

learn.title: Should the agent ask first, or just act?
learn.intro: Proactive agents from Anthropic, Meta and OpenAI are arriving fast, and each one forces the same call: which actions run on their own, and which wait for a yes.

columns.label: Let it act when
items: The result is a draft the person reviews, like a reply waiting to be sent
It only reads and summarises, like a morning brief of email and calendar
The step is easy to undo and lands where the person will look

columns.label: Make it ask when
items: It speaks for the person to someone else, like sending a message
It moves money, signs something or deletes data
It would mark work as done; let only the person close a task

examples.name: Claude Duet
examples.text: Drafts replies for review, asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes, and leaves finishing a task to you.

learn.rule: If it can't be undone or speaks for the person, ask first, and always offer a stop that keeps finished work.
learn.take: The columns are our framing, built from Duet's published rules and Jakob Nielsen's guidance on stopping AI agents.
